sections.title: Markets
sections.body:
**Markets — Saturday 15 August 2026**

The week closes on a softer note after Thursday's record highs. The macro picture shifted on Friday: 
a preliminary University of Michigan reading showed Americans grew more pessimistic on the economy, with inflation remaining top of mind
 — enough to dampen the disinflation euphoria that drove Thursday's S&P 500 record. 
A softer-than-expected July retail sales report added to the caution, with headline sales falling 0.6% against expectations of a 0.1% gain.
 
The S&P 500 slipped around 0.2% but still capped its third consecutive weekly gain.


**FTSE / Europe** — 
London closed mixed on Friday, with weak mining and pharmaceutical stocks dragging the FTSE 100 down 22 points to 10,750.
 
Antofagasta fell 4.6% for a second day after Thursday's lowered production guidance; GSK and AstraZeneca both dropped 2.1%.
 
For the week, the FTSE 100 was down 1.4%
 — a notably poor showing against a broadly positive global backdrop.

**Japan** — 
The Nikkei 225 opened flat as the Bank of Japan signalled faster rate hikes
, capping the week's AI-driven rally. IJPN's -0.60% in the pre-fetch reflects that BoJ headwind.

**Sam's portfolio** — AMD's +6.50% is the standout mover. 
Super Micro Computer beat earnings expectations by 84% and CoreWeave's sales forecast also topped estimates
 — when two major AI infrastructure names lift forward shipment expectations in the same week, 
investors typically reprice the chip suppliers, which explains the concurrent gains in AMD.
 Defence names (BAE +0.98%, Rolls-Royce +1.05%, Chemring +1.29%) have recovered Friday's dip from yesterday's briefing, suggesting the profit-taking was shallow.

sections.title: Fantasy Premier League
sections.body:
**Deadline: GW1 — Friday 21 Aug, 17:30 BST**

**Prices**

Prices are locked until after the GW1 deadline. Nothing actionable here.

**Injuries — what's new**

The Brighton situation has crystallised since yesterday. 
Minteh's leg injury from the Roma friendly leaves Hurzeler without both first-choice wingers, as Mitoma is still recovering from hamstring surgery that ruled him out of the World Cup.
 This is no longer a "wait and see" — 
Mitoma has missed all of pre-season with no clear return date.
 
Brighton are expected to be without Mitoma, Baleba, and Ferguson for the opening weeks.


The FPL consequence: Gomez's case as a Brighton differential is now even stronger than it was yesterday, since both wide options ahead of him are gone.

Elsewhere, two flagged players from the pre-fetched data worth noting:

- **Mukiele** (Sunderland, 4.3% owned) — 
Sunderland manager Le Bris confirmed Mukiele picked up a minor injury in pre-season but expects both him and Alderete "on the bench against Ipswich" in GW1
 — so a starter he is not.
- **Šeško** (Man Utd, 2.1% owned) — 
Šeško can still become available but should not be treated as a guaranteed GW1 starter yet.
 
Bruno Fernandes remains the safest Man Utd pick; wait for final evidence before selecting Šeško.


**Differentials**

Nothing new beyond what you already have on Havertz, Tavernier, Schade, and Vuskovic. 
Havertz remains the standout differential pick at just 6.9% ownership.
 
Vuskovic is also still in circulation — Brighton's new signing posted six goals and two assists in the Bundesliga last season.
 Ironic given the injury crisis around him; a clean sheet upside pick rather than an attacking one.

**Watch today:** any Minteh scan result from Brighton — if it confirms a multi-week absence, Gomez's ownership will move fast before Friday's deadline.

sections.title: Data & BI
sections.body:
**Data & BI**

**Power BI — legacy Excel/CSV import hard stop is today.** The three-stage retirement of the browser-based Excel/CSV import path reaches its final deadline. 
New models using that path were blocked in May; existing models stopped refreshing on 31 July; and from 31 August, reports built on those legacy models fail to open entirely.
 If anyone in your org still has a dashboard "looking a bit stale," this is the likely cause. The fix is straightforward: 
open Desktop, connect to the same file via Get Data, publish a new semantic model, and rebind the affected reports.


**Power BI — visual calculations hit GA.** Quietly landed alongside the July release: 
visual calculations are now generally available, making it easier to add DAX calculations directly to the visual where they're used
 rather than polluting the model with single-purpose measures.

**Power BI — .pbix download behaviour changed.** Worth flagging if developers are confused: 
downloading a .pbix from a semantic model in the Service now yields an empty report with the dataset only; to get the report with the dataset, you must go to the report itself — a change made to address inconsistent results from the old behaviour.


**BigQuery — data clean room query templates GA.** 
Query templates for data clean rooms are now generally available in BigQuery.
 Low fanfare, but useful if your org is doing any privacy-safe data collaboration with external partners.

**dbt Summit — early-bird pricing expires Monday.** 
The conference runs 15–18 September in Las Vegas; standard registration is $1,695 until 17 August, rising to $1,895 from the 18th.
 Worth knowing if the team has budget to burn before end of month.

sections.title: Career & Data Leadership
sections.body:
**Head of Data pay — cleaner floor figure**


[Bristow Holland](https://www.bristowholland.com/insights/industry-insights/uk-data-analytics-salary-expectations-in-2026-hiring-trends-and-workforce-planning/) puts Head of Data and data management leadership roles as frequently exceeding £90,000, particularly where responsibility covers governance, reporting strategy, and enterprise data architecture.
 That sits below the Director band covered yesterday (£87k–£142k) and gives a cleaner floor for the step you're targeting.

**Candidate mobility is notably high**


[Digital Waffle](https://www.digitalwaffle.co/salary-guides) reports that 66% of data specialists are open to new opportunities this year
 — well above most professional cohorts. For someone at Head of Data level, that means the external market is liquid and worth benchmarking against actively, not just at annual review.

**Salary growth in data is outpacing the broader tech market**


Salaries are rising 2–4% on average across tech, but data, AI, and cybersecurity are seeing growth of up to 6%.
 
Randstad Digital attribute this to a distinct scarcity of digital expertise, driving sharply rising and highly competitive salaries particularly for leadership roles in AI, Cloud, and Data.


**The visible-leadership risk**

A sharp framing from [The Executive Outlook](https://theexecutiveoutlook.com/blogs/effective-data-leadership-tips-lead-drive-impact-2026) worth sitting with: 
the defining risk for data leaders in 2026 is invisibility — technical credibility is no longer sufficient, and many leaders invest heavily in platforms before building organisational confidence in what those platforms produce.
 
Effective data leadership doesn't stop at the boundary of the data function; the impact ceiling of any data programme is set by the analytical capability of the business leaders consuming its output.
 Useful interview framing: what's your answer when the board asks what you've actually delivered?

**Delivery frameworks as a differentiator**


[Analytics8](https://www.analytics8.com/blog/ai-and-data-strategy-in-2026-what-leaders-need-to-get-right/) argues data leaders should prioritise scalable, repeatable delivery frameworks — defining clear steps from intake to execution to adoption, and aligning every project to a specific business problem with a measurable definition of success.
 The implication: "we shipped a platform" is a weak leadership story; "we changed how the business makes decisions" is the strong one.
